label: step after q in a d-initial sequence, late original phase (often input 2)
explanation: Very sparse feature (~0.006% of steps). Fires only in the original phase at steps 4-7 (peaking at t=5) and occasionally at the <DEL> step; it never fires in the copy phase. The main cues stack together: the sequence starts with d (87% of activation mass), the previous input is q (70% of mass), and the current input is 2 (60% of mass). The strongest activations have all three, e.g. d e q q [2]. Magnitude is highest when d-first, prev q and in 2 co-occur, and it falls off when any one of them is missing. Weak activations also appear with q two steps back, v in the prefix, or a non-d start. The predicate catches about 58% of mass, but precision is only about 0.1: most d...q contexts at steps 4-7 do not fire, and no simple extra condition separates them. That points to a fragile conjunction of cues rather than one clean concept.
